rationale: The book's core identification of the harlot as unfaithful Jerusalem (the covenant-breaker wearing covenant form without substance, the great city of Rev 17:18 identified via Rev 11:8's 'where also our Lord was crucified' and the OT harlot-Jerusalem pattern of Ezek 23:19 etc.) is the identification that best unifies the supplied texts without contradiction. It alone explains why the great city can be called both the harlot (covenant-specific adultery language) and the site of the crucifixion while inheriting the prophetic marriage-metaphor charges of bloodguilt and spiritual Sodom/Egypt. The strongest specific alternative (imperial Rome as the city that rules the kings of the earth) accounts for hills, commerce, and first-century power but requires extra steps to import covenant-harlot language and blood-of-prophets language that the OT and Jesus repeatedly fix on Jerusalem; those steps are less economical than the book's direct textual links. Secondary elaborations (seven-mountain western bloc, full Exodus-rod-serpent arc, precise modern geography) are not required for the core and remain under-determined, so support is limited to the core.
book_core_identification: The harlot is Jerusalem unfaithful—the covenant people/city that retains the form of the covenant while abandoning its substance, identified as 'that great city' of Revelation 17:18 via the spiritual names Sodom/Egypt and the crucifixion site of Revelation 11:8, continuing the OT pattern of Jerusalem as harlot (Ezekiel 23 etc.).
book_secondary_elaborations: The woman is the serpentine priesthood (Aaron's rod cast down that swallows the nations' rods) riding the beast of seven heads/mountains
The last Babylon is a westernmost seven-mountain bloc (Jeremiah 50:12 'hindermost' = western, with a base of power in the westernmost nation)

Full scene-for-scene Exodus typology (plagues, two witnesses as Moses/Aaron credentials, rod-serpent-rod-almond, sinking stone/millstone, song of Moses + Lamb) as the governing similitude of the Fall of Babylon
The forehead name is the counterfeit seal; the tail/liar-prophet mechanism and chazaq grip restore the rod
strongest_counter_interpretation: The harlot of Revelation 17–18 is specifically the city and empire of Rome (with its imperial cult, luxury commerce, and persecution), the dominant historical-critical and many patristic reading; the OT harlot language is applied analogically or typologically to any idolatrous/worldly power, not requiring a literal covenant-people referent.
counter_core_identification: Harlot = imperial Rome (the great city that reigns over the kings of the earth, sitting on seven hills, drunk with the blood of saints, center of global trade and luxury).
material_core_denial: Rome is not the covenant city that can commit true harlotry, is not the site 'where also our Lord was crucified,' and is not the city the prophets and Jesus repeatedly charge with the blood of the prophets; therefore the woman cannot be both Rome and the unfaithful Jerusalem of the book's core.
counter_case: Revelation 17:9 ('seven mountains') and 17:18 ('great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth') fit first-century Rome better than first-century Jerusalem under Roman occupation
The commercial lament of Revelation 18 (merchants, shipmasters, luxury goods) matches Rome's Mediterranean trade empire far more closely than Jerusalem's economy
1 Peter 5:13 and early Christian usage treat 'Babylon' as a cipher for Rome; many church fathers and modern historical-critical scholars adopt the same referent
OT harlot language can be extended analogically to any seductive anti-God power (Tyre, Nineveh) without requiring the referent to be a covenant people
book_explanatory_advantages: Directly unites Revelation 17:18 with Revelation 11:8's explicit crucifixion-site identification of 'the great city' without forcing a dual-city or purely spiritualizing reading
Preserves the covenant-specific force of harlotry (only a wife can commit it; Isaiah 1:21, Ezekiel 16/23, Hosea) rather than diluting it into generic worldliness
Explains the bloodguilt charge (Revelation 18:24) by Jesus' own words that fix all righteous blood and the prophets' deaths on Jerusalem (Matthew 23:35–37; Luke 13:33)
Accounts for the spiritual names Sodom and Egypt applied to Jerusalem already in Isaiah 1 and Ezekiel 16/23, plus Paul's Galatians 4:25 bondage language for 'Jerusalem which now is'
Keeps the marriage-metaphor consistency across the whole biblical witness rather than switching referents mid-stream
counter_explanatory_advantages: Better fit for the seven hills and 'reigns over the kings of the earth' language in a first-century setting
Superior match for the global commercial/luxury inventory of Revelation 18
Aligns with the dominant historical-critical and much patristic tradition that reads Babylon as Rome
decisive_sources: Revelation 11:8 (great city spiritually Sodom and Egypt where the Lord was crucified)
Matthew 23:35–37; Luke 13:33 (prophet-blood and death fixed on Jerusalem)
Revelation 18:24 (blood of prophets and saints found in her)
unresolved_objections: How a first-century or post-70 Jerusalem can be said to 'reign over the kings of the earth' without additional symbolic or post-70 expansion steps
Whether the commercial catalog of Revelation 18 fits Jerusalem as well as it fits Rome without further elaboration
The precise mapping of seven mountains and 'hindermost/western' geography remains secondary and under-determined by the core texts alone
